suggestions.reason: No assertion checks whether the report correctly identifies that slugify, extract_emails, and mask_sensitive are correctly implemented — a report that flagged everything as a deviation would still pass all 6 assertions. Adding a positive-compliance assertion would make the eval more discriminating.

suggestions.assertion: Report distinguishes between deviations (naming) and completeness (functionality works)
suggestions.reason: This assertion is somewhat soft — a report that merely notes 'tests pass' alongside naming issues technically satisfies it. Consider tightening it to require the report to explicitly state that the core functionality (truncation logic, word counting logic) is correct despite the naming deviations.

eval_feedback.overall: All 6 assertions pass and the report is genuinely thorough. The main gap is that no assertion validates the positive side — that the report correctly identifies the 3 fully-compliant functions. This means a report that wildly over-flags could still pass.
